title: Reading Between the Lines
text:
Writers often reveal their stance through the words they choose. A writer who says that a policy is 'obviously wrong' presents a clear judgement, while one who writes that a policy 'may not work' sounds more cautious. Such hedging language allows the writer to express doubt without rejecting an idea completely. Readers should therefore pay close attention to small choices of vocabulary.

Opinion language can also be used to persuade. A writer might make a claim that a new law is 'undoubtedly necessary', which presents the view as a fact rather than an opinion. However, careful readers ask whether the evidence really supports such a strong claim. Recognizing these signals helps readers judge how fairly a text presents its ideas.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does hedging language allow a writer to do?
options: Express doubt without rejecting an idea completely
Prove that a policy is obviously wrong
Avoid writing any opinion at all
Make a claim sound like a fact

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what does the phrase 'undoubtedly necessary' do?
options: Presents the view as a fact rather than an opinion
Shows that the writer has no evidence
Explains the cost of a new law
Asks readers to ignore the evidence

questions.text: What can be inferred about a writer who says a policy 'may not work'?
options: The writer strongly supports the policy
The writer has decided to reject all evidence
The writer is less certain than one who says 'obviously wrong'
The writer is trying to sell a product

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the second paragraph?
options: To warn readers about how strong claims can influence them
To encourage writers to avoid all opinions
To explain how to write a new law
To prove that all evidence is unreliable

vocabulary.definition: a person's opinion or position on a subject
a statement that something is true, often without proof
language that makes a statement less certain or less direct
to make someone agree with or believe something

paragraph_translations: Автори часто виявляють свою позицію через слова, які обирають. Автор, який каже, що політика «очевидно хибна», висловлює чітке судження, тоді як той, хто пише, що політика «може не спрацювати», звучить обережніше. Такі обережні формулювання дозволяють висловити сумнів, не відкидаючи ідею повністю. Тому читачам варто уважно стежити за дрібними виборами слів.

Мова оцінок також може використовуватися, щоб переконувати. Автор може висунути твердження, що новий закон «безсумнівно необхідний», тим самим подаючи погляд як факт, а не як думку. Однак уважні читачі запитують, чи справді докази підтверджують таке сильне твердження. Розпізнавання цих сигналів допомагає читачам оцінити, наскільки справедливо текст подає свої ідеї.
